definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese food made from wheat gluten that has been kneaded, shaped, and then baked or toasted until dry and light. Sold in hard, spongy pieces (rounds, sticks, or small flower shapes) that are rehydrated and added to soups, stews, sukiyaki, and simmered dishes.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{焼|や}き→焼く：01123_yaku⟧ (baked; toasted) and ⟦{麩|ふ}→麩：24202_fu⟧ (wheat gluten). One of several varieties of ⟦{麩|ふ}→麩：24202_fu⟧, distinguished from ⟦{生麩|なまふ}→生麩：23651_namafu⟧ (fresh wheat gluten, soft and chewy) and {揚|あ}げ{麩|ふ} (fried wheat gluten).

USAGE:
A common food word used in cookbooks, restaurant menus, and supermarket labels. Comes dried and must be soaked in water (or directly in broth) before cooking. Popular shapes include {小町麩|こまちふ} (small round pieces), ⟦{車麩|くるまふ}→車麩：08113_kurumafu⟧ (large wheel-shaped rounds from the Hokuriku region), and {花麩|はなふ} (small flower-shaped pieces, often dyed pink or green). In everyday conversation people often just say ⟦{麩|ふ}→麩：24202_fu⟧ when the context is clear.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {焼|や}き{麩|ふ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{水|みず}→水：02258_mizu⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{戻|もど}す→戻す：02317_modosu⟧: to rehydrate yaki-fu in water

- ⟦すき{焼|や}き→すき焼き：10368_sukiyaki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{焼|や}き{麩|ふ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{入|い}れる→入れる：01098_ireru⟧: to add yaki-fu to sukiyaki
- {焼|や}き{麩|ふ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{煮物|にもの}→煮物：04971_nimono⟧: simmered yaki-fu dish

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{生麩|なまふ}→生麩：23651_namafu⟧: fresh wheat gluten — soft, chewy, refrigerated; used in high-end cuisine and Buddhist temple food
- {揚|あ}げ{麩|ふ}: fried wheat gluten — deep-fried for a crispier texture
- ⟦{車麩|くるまふ}→車麩：08113_kurumafu⟧: wheel-shaped yaki-fu — a regional type, especially from Niigata
- グルテン: gluten — the general protein, not the food product
